title: Spoken greeting in Creole to Rolf's wife
summary: Guesnon addresses Rolf's wife in Creole, says the good old days in New Orleans are gone, and invites them back.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: 된 된 My demoiselle Daniel Roth. He sits at Josh Gano from the Novel of León. He says, hello, my friend. How are you? I understand, young lady, that you also are a friend of mine, so I'll dress you in my Creole tongue. I hope that you are fine and well and continue to enjoy all the best that's in life. I've got your husband here, and I'm giving a few pointers on the trumpet. And if you're the nice person that he is, then I will say that you're all really and truly a nice couple. He's a fine and swell guy, and I like him very much. I hope the time will come when there's a possibility that you both may be able to return to New Orleans and find some enjoyment. Of course, the good old days, like I was just explaining your husband, is no longer here. What is left is only a shell. But still and all for young people, they can come down here to play as long as we're alive. And I hope, as I said before, that you're enjoying all that is of the best. Mon ami, bon sent. Until we meet again. This is Creole George Gano of New Orleans, Louisiana.
